interpretation: These findings describe their actual endpoints. None supplies normalized bite probability or a calibrated local nearshore thermal-fit curve. A null curve is unavailable, never zero suitability.

species.endpoint: Agency cold-water ranges, laboratory optimum and field thermal occupancy
species.finding: Agency summaries span roughly 4.4-12.8 C or 9-11 C; a laboratory-derived 10 C optimum is not identical to seasonally realized habitat. Adult depth selection can separate fish from pier-reachable surface water.
species.transferDecision: Do not turn offshore habitat, stocking, or cold-water preference into a pier bite-response peak.

species.endpoint: Adult telemetry, depth/temperature experience and inferred foraging activity
species.finding: Eastern Lake Ontario/Trent River annual movements distinguish cool-season low activity from warmer-season activity. A cited growth optimum near 21 C is not a measured angling optimum.
species.transferDecision: No night-fishing bonus or numerical thermal response can be calibrated for these piers from telemetry alone.

species.endpoint: Guided fly-fishing catch rate versus noon temperature; separate laboratory preference/habitat synthesis
species.finding: The Wisconsin river study finds a positive temperature-catch association after skill correction. This is a relevant angling endpoint, but it is specific to three rivers, guided fly fishing and the sampled seasons.
species.transferDecision: Retain as a directional research hypothesis. No transferable Lake Michigan pier ordinates, optimum plateau or descending warm limb was established; do not manufacture them from laboratory preference.

species.endpoint: Species biology, spawning and historical Lake Erie growth
species.finding: The available numerical temperatures concern reproduction and growth, not targeted pier catch per hour. A summer growth maximum does not establish a thermal bite peak or annual response.
species.transferDecision: No numerical nearshore thermal-fit curve justified. Keep harbor-face representation unresolved where local reports describe channel fishing.

species.endpoint: General agency preference and behavior; assessment catchability study
species.finding: USGS describes moderate preference at 19-21 C and winter activity. These broad statements do not establish a 19-21 C pier-catch optimum, while spring pier catches occur outside a simple summer preference interpretation.
species.transferDecision: Do not penalize evidence-backed spring perch using a summer-growth or preference-only curve; local season, size selection and reachable-water response need calibration.

species.endpoint: Northwestern Lake Michigan thermal occupancy from recovered archival tags
species.finding: Of 400 tagged fish in 2017, 13 recovered records covered approximately 11 months. Reported summer mean was 10.8 C, with substantial time outside the literature's 10-14 C range. This is occupied temperature, not a feeding or angling experiment.
species.transferDecision: Neither summer occupancy nor autumn spawning establishes lawful November pier bite response; no shared curve with round whitefish.

species.endpoint: Agency seasonal movement and feeding description
species.finding: Michigan describes shallow spring/autumn use and reduced feeding around spawning. Shallow spawning occupancy therefore cannot automatically produce peak bite opportunity.
species.transferDecision: No suitable adult pier thermal-response dataset established. Lake-whitefish thermal values are taxonomically inapplicable.

species.finding: Adult river fish use covered deep pools by day and may enter shallows at night. This is not a temperature experiment or a local pier season measurement.
species.transferDecision: No normalized curve from general warm-water biology, juvenile aquaculture feeding or survival tolerance; no added nighttime score variable.

species.endpoint: General Michigan agency activity and habitat description
species.finding: The agency describes greatest activity at 70-85 F (21.1-29.4 C) and continuing winter activity. Habitat statements emphasize protected shallow water; they do not quantify local angling catchability.
species.transferDecision: Do not set a universal 21-29 C bite plateau, winter zero, or copy smallmouth's river relationship. Current exact-pier response remains unresolved.
